input.quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs an initial five (5) year term (§ 11.1) and § 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency; nothing in §§ 3-4, Exhibit B or elsewhere lets Corio, the customer here, exit for convenience. No Customer convenience right in a multi-year committed term is walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback (which would still require a 60-90 day Corio exit). New § 11.2A supplies the preferred 30-day customer convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. It identifies Corio expressly as the customer entitled to terminate but deliberately uses lower-case "customer" rather than the capitalised defined term, because § 1.6 defines "CUSTOMER(S)" as Corio's own sublicensees - using that term would wrongly hand the termination right to third parties. Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right (§ 11.2 confines it to breach and insolvency), so that element is already met; § 11.1's 30-day non-renewal notice is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic handled under RENEWAL. Exhibit B's payment terms contain no early-termination or acceleration charge, and all existing mechanics are retained verbatim.

ops.text: 11.2A Termination for Convenience. Corio is the customer under this Agreement, and such customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a new Section 11.2A letting Corio, as the customer, terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, since the five-year term currently permits termination only for breach or insolvency; we can fall back to 60-90 days' notice if needed.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 11.2A giving Corio, as customer, a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
